Task: Write a quick note explaining why TCP differs from UDP.

TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is connection-oriented and ensures reliable, in-order delivery of data through mechanisms like a three-way handshake, acknowledgments, retransmissions, flow control, and congestion control. UDP (User Datagram Protocol), by contrast, is connectionless and “best effort”: it sends discrete packets (datagrams) without establishing a session, offers no built-in error checking or retransmission, and delivers lower latency at the cost of potential loss, duplication, or out-of-order arrival.
